# AGENTS.md — tmm

## Overview
TMM (Traffic Management Microkernel) is F5's software data-plane engine for the modular BIG-IP (mBIP) platform. It processes network traffic at high speed — handling L4–L7 protocols, SSL, DNS, policy enforcement, NAT, and more — and is deployed as a containerized service within the Kubernetes-based SPK/mBIP stack. Control-plane configuration is delivered via MCP and PBUF message handlers; the resulting runtime state drives the fast-path packet processing pipeline.

## Quick Reference
- **Language(s)**: C (primary, ~95%), Python (test tooling/scripts, ~4%), Bash (~1%)
- **Build System**: GNU Make + Docker toolchain container (`make start` → `make tmm`)
- **Runtime Environment**: Ubuntu 24.04-based container (`f5-runtime-base-ubuntu24-04`), deployed on Kubernetes (SPK/mBIP)
- **Test Framework**: Custom C unit test runner (`test/unit/obj_x86_64.gcovut/t`), pytest + Tao for SSA functional tests, Robot Framework for access tests

## Critical Constraints
These are things an AI MUST know to avoid generating broken code:

1. **TMM CANNOT be compiled outside the build container.** Always use `make tmm` (or `make debug`) from the repo root — this delegates to the Docker toolchain. Running `make -C src/compile` directly only works from inside the container (`make interactive`). Never suggest bare compiler invocations outside this context.

2. **TMM cannot be run directly — only via unit tests or SSA functional tests.** TMM requires `mapres` to map hugepages and set up hardware-accelerated networking. Do not attempt to run or configure the `tmm` or `mapres` binaries. Use `make unittest` or `make -C test/ssa_functional run` to exercise code.

3. **All type primitives must come from `src/sys/types.h`.** Use `UINT8`, `UINT32`, `UINT64`, `BOOL`, `INT32`, etc. — never use raw C types like `unsigned int` directly where these apply. The file also redefines `double` and `float` to struct wrappers (`__double`, `__float`) to prevent accidental floating-point use in the data path; do not `#include` system headers that conflict with this.

4. **All source files must be registered in `src/compile/filelist` (or a per-module `filelist.mk`).** The build system does not auto-discover `.c` files — a new file that is not added to the filelist will be silently excluded from the build.

5. **Functions must have a single return point; use `goto out` for early exits.** The exit label must be named `out`. This is a hard style requirement enforced by code review and the automated `clang-style-check` CI job.

6. **Build output must be verified by checking the artifact timestamp.** Do not treat a successful `make` exit as proof of a working build. The build is only successful when `src/compile/obj_x86_64.<debug|no_pgo>/tmm.{debug|no_pgo}` exists with an up-to-date modification time. Important errors appear at the **end** of build output — never `head` it.

7. **The TMM is OS-independent by design.** Do not `#include` system headers or introduce new library dependencies without explicit approval. Use the shim layer in `src/kern/` to access OS facilities. Do not replicate libc or syscall declarations in your own code.

8. **Run [pylint](https://pypi.org/project/pylint/) and [black](https://pypi.org/project/black/) against all generated _ssa-functional-tests_**.  Accept all recommended code changes.

9. **Initialize all variables declared on the stack in the unit test code.**  The unit test code is not performance critical but it is fragile and sensitive to minor changes in memory usage.

## Anti-Patterns — What NOT to Do

- **Do not use `L7_POLICY_ACTION_RESET`** — this action is deprecated (see `src/base/policy_bind.c:2791`). Use `shutdown+connection` instead.

- **Do not call `pool_add()` for next-hop routing entries** — in `src/mcp/db_route.c`, next-hop pools must be managed via `nh_pools` directly. The comment at line 250 explicitly forbids `pool_add` in that context.

- **Do not use `sa_trans_from_cookie_complete_deprecated()`** — this function in `src/base/sa_trans.c` is explicitly named deprecated and must not be called in new code. Use the non-deprecated `sa_trans_from_cookie_complete()` variant.

- **Do not use `//` single-line comments** — TMM uses `/* */` block comment style exclusively throughout all C source files.

- **Do not use `double` or `float` literals/variables directly** — `src/sys/types.h` redefines them to opaque struct wrappers. Use `DOUBLE` or `FLOAT` typedefs, or restructure to avoid floating-point entirely in data-path code.

- Use **BSD style** for C code.

- Keep lines **under 76 columns**.

- Use **4 spaces** for indentation, and **no tabs**.
  - Indent wrapped lines by two indents (8 spaces)

- When modifying code, **keep the style consistent with the existing code**.

- In conditional statements, use a parenthesis for non-trivial sub-clauses: ((a != NULL) || ready())

- **Do not hardcode version numbers in `docker_build/modules-libs.json.template`** — version strings must be sourced from `input-manifest.yml` via gomplate templating. Hardcoded versions break the stagebot automated update process.

## Key Entry Points

- **MCP control-plane message handlers**: `src/mcp/` — each `db_*.c` file handles a specific configuration object type (e.g., `db_net.c` for network interfaces, `db_route.c` for routing, `db_profile.c` for profiles)
- **PBUF declarative handlers**: `src/pbuf/` — handles the declarative configuration API layer
- **HUD filter pipeline**: `src/modules/hudfilter/` — all HUD (data-path) filter implementations; filters are chained via `src/modules/hudchain.c`
- **Plugin manager**: `src/modules/plugin_manager.c` — registers and drives all loadable modules/plugins
- **Type system**: `src/sys/types.h` — fundamental typedefs used across the entire codebase
- **Build registration**: `src/compile/filelist` (and per-module `filelist.mk`) — every `.c` file must be listed here

## Where to Find More
- Build & run instructions: [README.md](README.md)
- Coding conventions: [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md)
- Architecture: [ARCHITECTURE.md](ARCHITECTURE.md)
- Test context: [TEST-CONTEXT.md](TEST-CONTEXT.md)
